method.procedure: requirements/benches.md#Receive ports and ticks on the Nucleo-F401RE
requirements/benches.md#Receive ports and ticks on the Nucleo-F401RE

conditions.image: release profile, thumbv7em-none-eabihf, no extra features; firmware hash not captured
conditions.links: FerroHAL's F401 links J1 (PA9-PA10) and J2 (PA11-PA12) fitted; PA9 and PA11 driven as GPIO by the firmware
equipment: Nucleo-F401RE (MB1136) through its ST-LINK V2-1, probe 0674FF555185754867115446

measurements.clocks: sysclk 84 MHz, pclk1 42 MHz, pclk2 84 MHz
measurements.ticks_200ms: TIM4 200 (0 gaps, last 200), TIM3 50 (0 gaps, last 50)
measurements.usart1_8e2: 1024 bytes read, 0 wrong, 0 gaps, 71 wakes (63 idle); every health counter 0
measurements.usart6_8n1: 1024 bytes read, 0 wrong, 0 gaps, 71 wakes (63 idle); every health counter 0

observations: Run by an agent on ubuntu-beefcake at the coordinator's board grant, from a fresh clone at this revision, through FerroHAL's rig telemetry wrapper (ferrohal-stm32 main fc8cef8).

Every member's vector was enabled; both timers ticked at their rates with no gap; on both ports every byte came back once and in order and the reader woke on idle lines; the firmware exited through semihosting with success.
limitations: Built and run from revision a99905e, the commit this record is made at.
The rig telemetry entry misattributes branch and commit (FerroHAL's), board name and probe, and has no build or flash timings, because the wrapper was pointed at another repository's script.
The RTT log stayed on the rig PC and is not attached; the figures above are as the runner reported them.
